subject.title: Memory compaction blocks main processing lane, causing unresponsive bot for 10+ minutes

question: Should compaction and memoryFlush move to an isolated or preemptible maintenance path, or remain serialized with foreground session turns plus shorter recovery limits?
rationale: The source-reproducible problem is real, but changing the lane boundary changes session ordering, transcript rotation, cancellation, and channel UX semantics; automation should not choose that architecture without maintainer intent.

options.title: Design maintenance isolation
options.body: Move or preempt compaction and memoryFlush with explicit ordering, cancellation, and recovery semantics so foreground messages can be acknowledged or processed promptly.

options.title: Limit to recovery mitigation
options.body: Keep compaction serialized but shorten timeouts/watchdog recovery, accepting that same-session messages still wait while maintenance is legitimately active.

options.title: Keep current serialization
options.body: Treat the blocking behavior as the cost of strict per-session safety and close only after documenting that tradeoff clearly for operators.

recommendation.title: Design maintenance isolation
recommendation.body: Move or preempt compaction and memoryFlush with explicit ordering, cancellation, and recovery semantics so foreground messages can be acknowledged or processed promptly.

likelyOwner.reason: Vincent Koc is the strongest current-history owner across the reply path, queued compaction wrapper, and diagnostic recovery code touched by any fix shape.
